notes: Phase 4: three-modality batch matrix (nano / small_molecule / biologic), 100 candidates total. Batches with a verbatim 'focus' string use it as-is; batches with 'description' instead get the flagship/prohibition constraint sentence generated from allow_cu_flagship. Optional 'modality_focus' per batch: 'nano_mixed' | 'small_molecule' | 'biologic' | a single schema_v2.MODALITIES value | null — drives the v2 CDA format block (schema_v2.cda_format_block). Pre-Phase-4 nano-only 4-batch config preserved in pipeline_config.nano_only.json (regression baseline). | 2026-07-25: expert chunks 2->4 — v2 records are longer (~200 chars), 60-line chunks hit the prompt[:10000] truncation and long inputs push report-trained adapters into prose mode.

batches.focus: Cu-based materials (any structural family). Assign EVERY material in this batch Disease_Intervention=direct_antibacterial AND Mechanism=microbiome_remodeling — the flagship selective-antibacterial, microbiome-remodeling Cu candidates (Cu2+/Cu+ redox cycling, pathogen-selective killing, beneficial-flora sparing, SCFA restoration)

mixed materials across varied elements (Fe, Co, Mn, Ni, Zn, Mo, and a FEW Cu). Cu-based materials are welcome but must NOT dominate this batch. Do NOT assign direct_antibacterial together with microbiome_remodeling in this batch

batches.description: small-molecule drug candidates relevant to Alzheimer's disease — prioritize marketed/clinical/literature-reported AD-related small molecules (e.g., donepezil, memantine, natural products). The compound NAME MUST be a real, verifiable compound and each candidate MUST give the UniProt accession of its primary protein target. SMILES: provide the canonical SMILES ONLY if you are completely certain of it; otherwise write NA — NEVER invent, guess, or repeat SMILES strings (a database lookup resolves SMILES from the compound name later). Mechanism assignments may include amyloid_tau_direct, neuroinflammation, microbiome_remodeling, etc.

biologic candidates relevant to Alzheimer's disease as reported in literature or clinical development — monoclonal antibodies, peptides, proteins (e.g., aducanumab, lecanemab, and other investigational biologics). Each candidate MUST have the UniProt accession of its primary protein target (Target_UniProt)
